passages.text: Paul came to Derbe and then to Lystra, where he found a disciple named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father.
passages.sermon:
Paul traveled to Derbe.
Paul then traveled to Lystra.
In Lystra, Paul found a disciple.
The disciple’s name was Timothy.
Timothy’s mother was a Jewish woman who believed in God.
Timothy’s father was a Greek.
passages.original: Κατήντησεν δὲ καὶ εἰς Δέρβην καὶ εἰς Λύστραν καὶ ἰδοὺ μαθητής τις ἦν ἐκεῖ ὀνόματι Τιμόθεος υἱὸς γυναικὸς Ἰουδαίας πιστῆς πατρὸς δὲ Ἕλληνος

passages.text: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.
passages.sermon: The brothers lived in Lystra and Iconium.\r\nThey spoke well of Timothy.\r\nThey gave him a good reputation.
passages.original: ὃς ἐμαρτυρεῖτο ὑπὸ τῶν ἐν Λύστροις καὶ Ἰκονίῳ ἀδελφῶν

passages.text: Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, so he took him and circumcised him on account of the Jews in that area, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle.
Timothy was a disciple.
Timothy’s mother was a believing Jewish woman.
Timothy’s father was a Greek.
Paul wanted Timothy to travel with him.
Paul took Timothy.
Paul circumcised Timothy.
Paul did this because of the Jews in that area.
All the people there knew Timothy’s father was a Greek.
passages.original: τοῦτον ἠθέλησεν ὁ Παῦλος σὺν αὐτῷ ἐξελθεῖν καὶ λαβὼν περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν διὰ τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς ὄντας ἐν τοῖς τόποις ἐκείνοις ᾔδεισαν γὰρ ἅπαντες ὅτι Ἕλλην ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ὑπῆρχεν

passages.text: As they went from town to town, they delivered the decisions handed down by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the people to obey.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions traveled from town to town.
They gave the people instructions to obey.
The apostles and elders in Jerusalem had decided these instructions.
Paul and his companions told the people to keep these decisions.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ διεπορεύοντο τὰς πόλεις παρεδίδοσαν αὐτοῖς φυλάσσειν τὰ δόγματα τὰ κεκριμένα ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τῶν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις

passages.text: So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers.
passages.sermon: The churches are groups of Christians.\r\nThe churches became strong in their faith.\r\nThe churches increased in number every day.
passages.original: Αἱ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησίαι ἐστερεοῦντο τῇ πίστει καὶ ἐπερίσσευον τῷ ἀριθμῷ καθ’ ἡμέραν

passages.text: After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia, they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions were traveling.
The Holy Spirit stopped them from speaking the word in the province of Asia.
They traveled through the region of Phrygia.
They also traveled through the region of Galatia.
passages.original: Διῆλθον δὲ τὴν Φρυγίαν καὶ Γαλατικὴν χώραν κωλυθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος λαλῆσαι τὸν λόγον ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ

passages.text: And when they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions traveled as missionaries.
They came to the border of Mysia.
They tried to go into Bithynia.
The Spirit of Jesus did not allow them to enter Bithynia.
passages.original: ἐλθόντες δὲ κατὰ τὴν Μυσίαν ἐπείραζον εἰς τὴν Βιθυνίαν πορευθῆναι καὶ οὐκ εἴασεν αὐτοὺς τὸ Πνεῦμα Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions traveled.
They did not stay in Mysia.
They passed by Mysia.
They went down to Troas.
passages.original: παρελθόντες δὲ τὴν Μυσίαν κατέβησαν εἰς Τρῳάδα

passages.text: During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian preacher and missionary.
One night, Paul saw a vision.
In the vision, a man from Macedonia stood before Paul.
The man pleaded with Paul.
The man said, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
passages.original: Καὶ ὅραμα διὰ τῆς νυκτὸς τῷ Παύλῳ ὤφθη ἀνὴρ Μακεδών τις ἦν ἑστὼς καὶ παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγων Διαβὰς εἰς Μακεδονίαν βοήθησον ἡμῖν

passages.text: As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.
passages.sermon:
Paul saw a vision at night.
The vision showed a man from Macedonia.
The man stood and pleaded with Paul.
He said, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
As soon as Paul saw the vision, we prepared to leave for Macedonia.
We believed that God had called us.
God called us to preach the gospel to the people in Macedonia.
passages.original: ὡς δὲ τὸ ὅραμα εἶδεν εὐθέως ἐζητήσαμεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς Μακεδονίαν συμβιβάζοντες ὅτι προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς εὐαγγελίσασθαι αὐτούς

passages.text: We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace, and the following day on to Neapolis.
passages.sermon: Paul and his companions left Troas.\r\nThey sailed directly to Samothrace.\r\nThe next day, they traveled to Neapolis.
passages.original: Ἀναχθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ Τρῳάδος εὐθυδρομήσαμεν εἰς Σαμοθρᾴκην τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ εἰς Νέαν Πόλιν

passages.text: From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi, the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions traveled to Philippi.
Philippi was a Roman colony.
Philippi was the leading city in that part of Macedonia.
They stayed in Philippi for several days.
passages.original: κἀκεῖθεν εἰς Φιλίππους ἥτις ἐστὶν πρώτη τῆς μερίδος Μακεδονίας πόλις κολωνία Ἦμεν δὲ ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ πόλει διατρίβοντες ἡμέρας τινάς

passages.text: On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate along the river, where it was customary to find a place of prayer. After sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions were in Philippi, a leading city in Macedonia.
On the Sabbath, we went outside the city gate.
We went to the river.
People usually gathered there to pray.
We sat down by the river.
Women had gathered there.
We spoke to the women.
passages.original: Τῇ τε ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ἐξήλθομεν ἔξω τῆς πύλης παρὰ ποταμὸν οὗ ἐνομίζομεν προσευχὴν εἶναι καὶ καθίσαντες ἐλαλοῦμεν ταῖς συνελθούσαις γυναιξίν

passages.text: Among those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.
passages.sermon:
A woman named Lydia was there.
Lydia sold purple cloth.
She came from the city of Thyatira.
Lydia worshiped God.
She listened to us.
The Lord opened Lydia’s heart.
She paid attention to what Paul said.
passages.original: Καί τις γυνὴ ὀνόματι Λυδία πορφυρόπωλις πόλεως Θυατείρων σεβομένη τὸν Θεόν ἤκουεν ἧς ὁ Κύριος διήνοιξεν τὴν καρδίαν προσέχειν τοῖς λαλουμένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου

passages.text: And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” And she persuaded us.
passages.sermon:
Lydia was a woman from the city of Thyatira.
She sold purple cloth.
She worshiped God.
The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.
Lydia and her household were baptized.
After this, Lydia spoke to us.
She said, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.”
She urged us strongly.
She persuaded us to stay.
passages.original: ὡς δὲ ἐβαπτίσθη καὶ ὁ οἶκος αὐτῆς παρεκάλεσεν λέγουσα Εἰ κεκρίκατέ με πιστὴν τῷ Κυρίῳ εἶναι εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου μένετε καὶ παρεβιάσατο ἡμᾶς

passages.text: One day as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions were going to the place of prayer.
A slave girl met them.
This girl had a spirit of divination.
She could tell fortunes.
She earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ πορευομένων ἡμῶν εἰς τὴν προσευχὴν παιδίσκην τινὰ ἔχουσαν πνεῦμα Πύθωνα ὑπαντῆσαι ἡμῖν ἥτις ἐργασίαν πολλὴν παρεῖχεν τοῖς κυρίοις αὐτῆς μαντευομένη

passages.text: This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!”
passages.sermon:
A slave girl met Paul and his companions.
This girl had a spirit of divination.
She followed Paul and the rest of us.
She shouted as she followed us.
She said, “These men are servants of the Most High God.”
She said, “They are proclaiming to you the way of salvation.”
passages.original: αὕτη κατακολουθοῦσα τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἡμῖν ἔκραζεν λέγουσα Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι δοῦλοι τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου εἰσίν οἵτινες καταγγέλλουσιν ὑμῖν ὁδὸν σωτηρίας

passages.text: She continued this for many days. Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” And the spirit left her at that very moment.
passages.sermon:
A slave girl had a spirit of divination.
She followed Paul and his companions.
She shouted about them for many days.
She kept doing this for a long time.
Paul became very troubled.
Paul turned to the spirit in the girl.
Paul spoke directly to the spirit.
Paul said, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I command you to come out of her.”
The spirit left the girl immediately.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ ἐποίει ἐπὶ πολλὰς ἡμέρας διαπονηθεὶς δὲ Παῦλος καὶ ἐπιστρέψας τῷ πνεύματι εἶπεν Παραγγέλλω σοι ἐν ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπ’ αὐτῆς καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ

passages.text: When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.
passages.sermon:
The girl’s owners saw that they could not make money from her anymore.
They lost their hope of profit.
They seized Paul and Silas.
They dragged Paul and Silas into the marketplace.
They brought Paul and Silas before the authorities.
passages.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ κύριοι αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐξῆλθεν ἡ ἐλπὶς τῆς ἐργασίας αὐτῶν ἐπιλαβόμενοι τὸν Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἵλκυσαν εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας

passages.text: They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice.”
passages.sermon:
Paul and Silas were followers of Jesus.
The owners of the slave girl brought Paul and Silas to the magistrates.
The magistrates were the city’s officials.
The owners spoke to the magistrates.
They said, “These men are Jews.”
They said, “They are causing trouble in our city.”
They said, “They teach customs.”
They said, “These customs are not lawful for us.”
They said, “We are Romans.”
They said, “We cannot accept or practice these customs.”
passages.original: καὶ προσαγαγόντες αὐτοὺς τοῖς στρατηγοῖς εἶπαν Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἐκταράσσουσιν ἡμῶν τὴν πόλιν Ἰουδαῖοι ὑπάρχοντες καὶ καταγγέλλουσιν ἔθη ἃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἡμῖν παραδέχεσθαι οὐδὲ ποιεῖν Ῥωμαίοις οὖσιν

passages.text: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Silas were Christian missionaries.
The crowd attacked Paul and Silas.
The magistrates gave an order.
The magistrates ordered that Paul and Silas be stripped of their clothes.
The magistrates ordered that Paul and Silas be beaten with rods.
passages.original: Καὶ συνεπέστη ὁ ὄχλος κατ’ αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ στρατηγοὶ περιρήξαντες αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐκέλευον ῥαβδίζειν

passages.text: And after striking them with many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Silas were followers of Jesus.
The magistrates ordered that Paul and Silas be beaten.
The officials struck Paul and Silas with many blows.
They threw Paul and Silas into prison.
The magistrates commanded the jailer to guard Paul and Silas securely.
passages.original: πολλάς τε ἐπιθέντες αὐτοῖς πληγὰς ἔβαλον εἰς φυλακήν παραγγείλαντες τῷ δεσμοφύλακι ἀσφαλῶς τηρεῖν αὐτούς

passages.text: On receiving this order, he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.
passages.sermon: The jailer received strict orders to guard Paul and Silas securely.\r\nHe put Paul and Silas into the inner cell of the prison.\r\nHe fastened their feet in the stocks.
passages.original: ὃς παραγγελίαν τοιαύτην λαβὼν ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν ἐσωτέραν φυλακὴν καὶ τοὺς πόδας ἠσφαλίσατο αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ ξύλον

passages.text: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Silas were in prison.
It was about midnight.
Paul and Silas prayed.
They sang hymns to God.
The other prisoners listened to them.
passages.original: Κατὰ δὲ τὸ μεσονύκτιον Παῦλος καὶ Σιλᾶς προσευχόμενοι ὕμνουν τὸν Θεόν ἐπηκροῶντο δὲ αὐτῶν οἱ δέσμιοι

passages.text: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison. At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.
passages.sermon:
A strong earthquake happened suddenly.
The earthquake shook the foundations of the prison.
All the doors opened immediately.
Everyone’s chains came loose.
passages.original: ἄφνω δὲ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας ὥστε σαλευθῆναι τὰ θεμέλια τοῦ δεσμωτηρίου ἠνεῴχθησαν δὲ παραχρῆμα αἱ θύραι πᾶσαι καὶ πάντων τὰ δεσμὰ ἀνέθη

passages.text: When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, presuming that the prisoners had escaped.
passages.sermon:
The jailer worked at the prison.
He woke up.
He saw that the prison doors were open.
He thought the prisoners had escaped.
He drew his sword.
He was about to kill himself.
passages.original: Ἔξυπνος δὲ γενόμενος ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ καὶ ἰδὼν ἀνεῳγμένας τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς σπασάμενος τὴν μάχαιραν ἤμελλεν ἑαυτὸν ἀναιρεῖν νομίζων ἐκπεφευγέναι τοὺς δεσμίους

passages.text: But Paul called out in a loud voice, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!”
passages.sermon:
Paul was a prisoner in the jail.
Paul saw the jailer about to harm himself.
Paul called out with a loud voice.
Paul said, “Do not harm yourself.”
Paul said, “We are all here.”
passages.original: ἐφώνησεν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος μεγάλῃ φωνῇ λέγων Μηδὲν πράξῃς σεαυτῷ κακόν ἅπαντες γάρ ἐσμεν ἐνθάδε

passages.text: Calling for lights, the jailer rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.
passages.sermon:
The jailer worked at the prison.
He called for lights.
He rushed into the prison.
He saw Paul and Silas.
He became very afraid.
He trembled.
He fell down before Paul and Silas.
passages.original: Αἰτήσας δὲ φῶτα εἰσεπήδησεν καὶ ἔντρομος γενόμενος προσέπεσεν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Σιλᾷ

passages.text: Then he brought them out and asked, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
passages.sermon: The jailer brought Paul and Silas outside.\r\nHe spoke to them.\r\nHe said, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
passages.original: καὶ προαγαγὼν αὐτοὺς ἔξω ἔφη Κύριοι τί με δεῖ ποιεῖν ἵνα σωθῶ

passages.text: They replied, “Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household.”
passages.sermon:
Paul and Silas spoke to the jailer.
They answered his question.
They said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus.”
If you believe in Jesus, you will be saved.
Your household will also be saved if they believe.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Πίστευσον ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν καὶ σωθήσῃ σὺ καὶ ὁ οἶκός σου

passages.text: Then Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Silas spoke to the jailer.
They told him the word of the Lord.
They also spoke to everyone in his house.
They shared the message with all who lived there.
passages.original: καὶ ἐλάλησαν αὐτῷ τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου σὺν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. And without delay, he and all his household were baptized.
passages.sermon:
The jailer took Paul and Silas at that hour of the night.
He washed their wounds.
He was baptized immediately.
All his household were baptized immediately.
passages.original: καὶ παραλαβὼν αὐτοὺς ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τῆς νυκτὸς ἔλουσεν ἀπὸ τῶν πληγῶν καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ αὐτοῦ πάντες παραχρῆμα

passages.text: Then he brought them into his home and set a meal before them. So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God.
passages.sermon:
The jailer believed in God.
He brought Paul and Silas into his home.
He set a meal before them.
He and his whole household rejoiced.
They all believed in God.
passages.original: ἀναγαγών τε αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν οἶκον παρέθηκεν τράπεζαν καὶ ἠγαλλιάσατο πανοικεὶ πεπιστευκὼς τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: When daylight came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: “Release those men.”
passages.sermon:
The magistrates held authority in the city.
Daylight came.
The magistrates sent their officers.
The magistrates gave a command.
They said, “Release those men.”
passages.original: Ἡμέρας δὲ γενομένης ἀπέστειλαν οἱ στρατηγοὶ τοὺς ῥαβδούχους λέγοντες Ἀπόλυσον τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἐκείνους

passages.text: The jailer informed Paul: “The magistrates have sent orders to release you. Now you may go on your way in peace.”
passages.sermon:
The jailer spoke to Paul.
He gave Paul a message from the magistrates.
The magistrates had sent orders.
They ordered that Paul and Silas should be released.
The jailer told Paul, “You may leave now.”
He said, “Go in peace.”
passages.original: Ἀπήγγειλεν δὲ ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ τοὺς λόγους τούτους πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον ὅτι Ἀπέσταλκαν οἱ στρατηγοὶ ἵνα ἀπολυθῆτε νῦν οὖν ἐξελθόντες πορεύεσθε ἐν εἰρήνῃ

passages.text: But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial and threw us into prison, even though we are Roman citizens. And now do they want to send us away secretly? Absolutely not! Let them come themselves and escort us out!”
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Roman citizen.
\r\nPaul spoke to the officers.
\r\nHe said, "They beat us in public."
\r\nThey did not give us a trial.
\r\nWe are Roman citizens.
\r\nThey put us in prison.
\r\nNow they want to send us away in secret.
\r\nThat is not right.
\r\nLet the magistrates come themselves.
\r\nLet them lead us out."
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη πρὸς αὐτούς Δείραντες ἡμᾶς δημοσίᾳ ἀκατακρίτους ἀνθρώπους Ῥωμαίους ὑπάρχοντας ἔβαλαν εἰς φυλακήν καὶ νῦν λάθρᾳ ἡμᾶς ἐκβάλλουσιν οὐ γάρ ἀλλὰ ἐλθόντες αὐτοὶ ἡμᾶς ἐξαγαγέτωσαν

passages.text: So the officers relayed this message to the magistrates, who were alarmed to hear that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.
passages.sermon:
The officers carried a message to the magistrates.
The message was about Paul and Silas.
Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.
The magistrates heard this news.
The magistrates became afraid.
passages.original: Ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ τοῖς στρατηγοῖς οἱ ῥαβδοῦχοι τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Ῥωμαῖοί εἰσιν

passages.text: They came to appease them and led them out, requesting that they leave the city.
passages.sermon:
The magistrates came to Paul and Silas.
The magistrates wanted to calm Paul and Silas.
The magistrates led Paul and Silas out of the prison.
The magistrates asked Paul and Silas to leave the city.
passages.original: καὶ ἐλθόντες παρεκάλεσαν αὐτούς καὶ ἐξαγαγόντες ἠρώτων ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως

passages.text: After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them. Then they left the city.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Silas left the prison.
They went to Lydia’s house.
They saw the brothers there.
They encouraged the brothers.
Then Paul and Silas left the city.
passages.original: ἐξελθόντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς φυλακῆς εἰσῆλθον πρὸς τὴν Λυδίαν καὶ ἰδόντες παρεκάλεσαν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἐξῆλθαν
